ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus jaintiaensis* reaches a snout-vent length of 70 mm. It is brown with dark dorsal bands and possesses 18–20 subdigital lamellae on the fourth toe and 12–14 precloacal pores in males.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus jaintiaensis* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 4–5 distinct, dark, wavy transverse bands that are narrower than the interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus jaintiaensis* inhabits the moist, subtropical broadleaf forests of the Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus jaintiaensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that remains hidden in rock crevices during the day to avoid predators and conserve moisture.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus jaintiaensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus jaintiaensis* is endemic to the Jaintia Hills in the state of Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits high-elevation rocky forest habitats.
